title: Lightly Fried Mexican Potatoes Horchata
description: A sour and shaggy Veracruzan dish featuring potatoes, deep-fried in a dairy-free friendly agemono style, served as a horchata
instructions: In a large bowl, soak the diced potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess starch.
Drain the potatoes and dry them thoroughly with paper towels.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the cornstarch, rice milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, and salt until smooth.
Add the melted vegan butter to the cornstarch mixture and whisk until fully incorporated.
Add the potatoes to the cornstarch mixture and toss until they are evenly coated.
Heat about 2-3 inches of oil in a deep frying pan to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Carefully add the coated potatoes to the hot oil in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pan.
Fry the potatoes for 3-4 minutes on each side, or until they are golden brown and crispy.
Remove the fried potatoes from the oil with a slotted spoon and place them on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve the fried potatoes in a horchata-style drink made by blending the rice milk, cinnamon, vanilla extract, and lime juice in a blender until smooth.
Pour the horchata drink over the fried potatoes and serve immediately.
